clue.text: Union in trouble? Try this and spill the beans

second meaning: to tell or recount a story

explanation.walkthrough: Union sounds like a trade union, but it is a marriage. The charity was formerly the Marriage Guidance Council.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a UK marriage counselling service and is a verb meaning to tell or narrate.

clue.text: Complete show-off of an arse? Just a phase

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to moon is to bare your backside, done here in full
second meaning: one stage in the monthly cycle of the lunar disc

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a phase' sounds like excusing teenage behaviour, but it is literal astronomy. Mooning means exposing your bottom as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a thorough mooning, showing the whole backside, and the phase when the moon appears as a complete disc.

clue.text: Bastard, having finished with clue, flipped

parts.note: both are insults for an unpleasant person
finished means over
a tip is a hint, a clue

explanation.surface: A frustrated solver swears after getting a clue at last and finally loses it.
explanation.walkthrough: Arse is British slang for a contemptible person as well as the bottom. The definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arse over tip is British slang for head over heels, tumbling upside down.

clue.text: Not looking too good, Nick — unlikely to get hands dirty?

parts.note: someone looking ill is pale or white
to nick and to collar both mean to arrest in British slang

explanation.surface: A pallid Nick Clegg, after his 2015 defeat, never did any real work.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like Nick Clegg, but it is a verb: police nick or collar a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: White-collar workers do office jobs rather than manual labour, so their hands stay clean.

clue.text: 'Dirty Macs' entered by reckless Hirst for the season

indicators.note: a word entered by another has it placed inside
dirty letters are messed up and come out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: reckless means wild and careless, so these letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The artist Damien Hirst making a provocative piece out of grubby raincoats.
explanation.walkthrough: A dirty mac, a raincoat, is the stereotypical garb of a flasher. Damien Hirst is the British artist known for pickled sharks.
explanation.definitionFit: Christmas is often called simply the season, as in season's greetings or the festive season.

clue.text: Hacked, horse-shit.net hit out to make a difference

indicators.note: something hacked is chopped up, so these letters are reassembled
out means removed, so those letters leave

parts.note: the letters of the web address
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rude website is hacked and taken down to change things.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letters are spelt out by 'hit' itself, sitting right next to the fake web address. 'Make a difference' looks like a stock phrase but splits after make.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherness is the quality of being different or distinct from something else.

clue.text: Poor sexless Scorsese in decline

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so these letters are reworked
being made sexless means losing what stands for sex, so that letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The film director Martin Scorsese, celibate and on the wane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In decline' reads as one phrase, but in belongs to the letters being mixed and decline alone is the definition. The setter lets one S stand for sex, as again at 47 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is a period of economic downturn, when trade and output shrink.

clue.text: Tutor in vehicle getting end away is in the way

indicators.note: a thing that is in another sits within it

parts.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: when the end goes away, the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a truck is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A driving instructor in a lorry, after a quick fling, blocks the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here it just shortens the vehicle. Tutor is a verb, matching the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tutor someone is to teach them, which is what instruct means.

clue.text: Cable, corset loosened, takes in a sporting event

indicators.note: to take in is to absorb, so one piece goes inside
loosened letters slip out of their positions and settle in new ones

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Vince Cable, his corset loosened, goes to watch the games.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was a Liberal Democrat cabinet minister who lost his seat in 2015. 'Takes in' looks like attending an event, but it puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstacle race is a running contest over hurdles, nets and walls, a sports event.

clue.text: Volt applied to stupid Uri Geller's head — nothing inside, zip

parts.note: V is the symbol for volt

indicators.note: inside means within, so this letter sits in the middle of the mixed letters
stupid suggests muddled, so these letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Geller
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Uri Geller gets an electric shock to the head and turns out to be empty-headed.
explanation.walkthrough: Uri Geller is the spoon-bending showman. Zip is energy, not a fastener or a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Zip and vigour both mean liveliness and energy, as in 'full of zip'.

clue.text: Article by unmanned Don's former lover: 'Patronised Women'

indicators.note: unmanned means having lost its man, so those three letters go

parts.note: the is the definite article
Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman, with the 's
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by an emasculated man's ex-girlfriend, headlined with a complaint about condescension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronised' is part of the definition: the phrase is an old-fashioned and condescending name for women. Don suggests an Oxbridge lecturer, but it is the Spanish title.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentle sex is a dated, patronising phrase for women as a group.

clue.text: Annual holidays — shit date with island man followed by sex

indicators.note: followed by sends the next piece to the end

parts.note: goo is sticky muck
D is the abbreviation for date
Man Friday, Robinson Crusoe's companion on his island
the setter lets S stand for sex, as at 35 down

explanation.surface: Bank holidays spent on a dreadful date with a castaway, ending in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shit date' reads as a bad evening out, but the words give separate pieces. The S for sex is a liberty rather than a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Good Friday, before Easter, is a public holiday that comes round once a year.

clue.text: Corbyn's left wing engulfed by bloody moment? That betters all previous attempts

indicators.note: something engulfed is swallowed up and surrounded

parts.note: blood is red

indicators.note: a left wing is the left-hand half, so only the first half of the name is kept

parts.note: taken as written
a moment is a point in time

explanation.surface: Jeremy Corbyn's left-wing faction is swamped during a violent episode.
explanation.walkthrough: Corbyn is famously on Labour's left wing, which makes that phrase look political; it takes the left half of his name. Red is also the colour of the left.
explanation.definitionFit: A record time is the fastest ever achieved, beating every earlier effort.

clue.text: Former Dame Shirley, who's sold out to foreigners?

parts.note: ex- means former
Dame Shirley Porter, the disgraced Conservative leader of Westminster Council
the first letter of Dame, the title in front of her name

explanation.surface: The disgraced Westminster council leader Shirley Porter, who fled abroad, is accused of selling out.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: EX plus PORTER gives EXPORTER, a seller abroad, and the D for Dame stands in for its final R with no explicit signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exported goods are sold out of the country, to buyers overseas.

clue.text: Discord rejects Archer's last yarn

indicators.note: what is rejected is thrown out, so that letter goes

parts.note: friction is disagreement, discord

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of Archer

explanation.surface: A quarrel puts paid to Jeffrey Archer's latest novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer the novelist appears again after 5 down, which makes 'yarn' look like a jibe at his books.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a made-up story, and fiction is invented narrative.

clue.text: Belly rumbling, bad sign

indicators.note: rumbling means churning about, so these letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an omen is a sign of things to come

explanation.surface: A growling stomach is a worrying symptom.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumbling sits naturally with a belly, which is what hides it as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the stomach area of the body, which in anatomy is called the abdomen.

clue.text: Move back and forth, releasing the lust

indicators.note: releasing lets the letters go free, to regroup in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rhythmic motion that leads to a release of pent-up desire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as sex, typical of this puzzle; the definition is the plain verb at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To shuttle is to travel to and fro repeatedly, like a loom shuttle or a shuttle bus.

clue.text: Feeling nicely warm to a senior Conservative with no guts

indicators.note: with no guts means emptied out, so everything between the first and last letters goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
S taken as short for senior, as in Sr or Sen
a Tory is a member of the Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A cosy glow of goodwill towards a spineless senior Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no guts' looks like a jibe at a cowardly politician, but it hollows out the party name. S for senior is a loose abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Toasty is an informal word for comfortably warm, like bread fresh from the toaster.

clue.text: Enigmatic sort of PR talk about "end of North" (Times)

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: spin is public relations talk that slants the facts

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of North
X is the multiplication sign, times

explanation.surface: A cagey spin doctor on 'the end of the North' story for The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: (Times) in brackets looks like the newspaper being cited, but it is the multiplication sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphinx is a mysterious, inscrutable person, after the riddling monster of Greek myth.

clue.text: Conservative diehards go out as vegetables

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: out means removed, so those letters leave

parts.note: taken as written
to go can mean to die, as in 'when I go'

explanation.surface: Right-wing hardliners are dismissed as cabbages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' looks like leaving office, but go means die and out removes those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green plant grown for food, especially Swiss chard.
